key_insight: Neptuna shows that no single surrogate model or loss function dominates shock-driven multiphase flow prediction, but composite losses and adaptive weighting can substantially improve interface and spectral accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This benchmark helps engineers compare machine learning surrogates for compressible multiphase flows more reliably, supporting faster design and analysis of bubble collapse and droplet breakup problems.
method: Large-scale benchmark with 2.4 TB of high-fidelity 2D and 3D shock-driven multiphase flow data
Evaluates convolutional, spectral, transformer-based, and pre-trained PDE foundation models
Tests MSE, Sobolev, interface-aware, and structure-aware losses with SoftAdapt and GradNorm
evidence_signal: The framework combines pointwise, spectral, feature-focused, structural, and physics-informed metrics, and the abstract reports that SoftAdapt gives the most consistent gains with minimal overhead.
watch_item: Performance varies across datasets and metrics, so reported gains may not transfer uniformly without careful model, loss, and task-specific tuning.
paper_title: Neptuna: A Comprehensive Machine Learning Framework for Benchmarking Complex Multiphase Flows
